items.context: Dating and social startup; in five months, sole engineer across the Flutter app, NestJS backend (180+ APIs, 1,066 automated tests), and Docker deployment, also taking over subscription billing (monthly revenue NT$210K → NT$380K), while maintaining two product lines (Sugarbee and Bound)
jobDesc: Commercializing AI: built match suggestions, chat coaching, icebreakers, and bio generation on the Anthropic API as paid subscription features — JSON-constrained structured output with de-identified inputs, regex filtering on outputs, three-tier merge-based degradation (AI output, profile templates, generic copy), and timeouts calibrated to production P95 (4.5s → 8s after Sonnet shipped).

AI quality and governance: built the RAG support agent in Python (FastAPI) without LangChain — hybrid retrieval with RRF fusion, LLM reranking, circuit breakers with provider failover — with a golden dataset and LLM-as-a-Judge putting Recall, MRR, and Groundedness in CI; also wrote the team's AI development standard: LLM calls must be awaited, fire-and-forget banned, background work through SQS, and AI never blocking payments, messaging, or matching.

Serverless architecture and production stability: backend on AWS Lambda (production reservedConcurrency 450) with RDS Proxy multiplexing connections, AI generation and video moderation through SQS with Firebase pushing results back, synchronous image moderation plus real-person face verification; traced a connection-count alert to pinned connections left by frozen Lambda containers, cutting peak connections from 1,162 to 883 (−24%) and establishing the rule that a frozen container is not a finished process.

Performance and cost: replaced runtime JSON parsing in the recommendation query with MySQL virtual generated columns and composite indexes (5s → milliseconds, core APIs averaging 180ms); a distributed lock before generation plus two-tier caching tied AI cost to generations rather than views, and moving static traffic to S3 + CDN with database right-sizing cut monthly cloud spend from US$1,200 to US$400 (−60%), with FCP going from 10s to 1.4s.

items.context: Game and live-streaming platform; joined in 2020 as a backend engineer, promoted in late 2022 to lead 11 engineers across architecture and technical decisions for 12 product lines
jobDesc: Split each game format into API, Socket, business service, and async consumer, carrying peak-hour draw traffic of a thousand bets/orders per second and scaling at whichever tier is the bottleneck; Kafka for cross-service event streams, Redis and Bull Queue for caching and async settlement, Socket.IO for live rounds and draw results.
Took a proof-of-concept mini-game to production, then reused its shared services and delivery process across later titles, leading the team to 12 shipped product lines.

Added monitoring and logging (Sentry, Kibana, Grafana) and turned recurring troubleshooting into docs and saved queries, cutting problem isolation time by about 50%; turning release steps into a checklist and documented process reduced release defects by 70%.
Introduced design review before work starts and code review before merge so design and implementation defects are caught pre-release; both became the shared standard across product lines.

items.context: Same company, pre-promotion role; backend development and system analysis on a game and lottery platform, including taking over an unmaintained legacy system
jobDesc: Lead backend on the blockchain fair-random-number platform: combined multiple data sources into verifiable random numbers and wrote EOS smart contracts for on-chain proof, letting players verify draw results themselves.
Refactored an unmaintained inherited system into layered modules with shared logic extracted, so new game types extend the existing architecture without touching the core settlement flow.
Used slow-query logs to locate reporting and settlement bottlenecks, then added indexes and reworked queries and pagination, eliminating query timeouts during batch settlement.
Sole owner of lottery game types, the crawler data pipeline, and the operations dashboard — schema design through production operations.

items.context: Software consultancy; delivered 7 client engagements spanning requirements analysis through production operations
jobDesc: Delivered lending, video streaming, equipment repair, and e-commerce systems from zero to one — requirements analysis, system design, through production operations.
Moved transcoding and image blurring to AWS Lambda + FFmpeg as async jobs so long-running work no longer occupied application servers, and replaced manual releases with automated deployment.
Split frontend/backend responsibilities and redesigned APIs to cut coupling so both sides could work in parallel, with unit and functional tests covering regression after changes.
Chose stacks by the client's existing environment and timeline (C#, Node.js, React, Salesforce), extending current systems instead of rebuilding them.
